issues.legal_issue: Whether the evidence established that a temple associated with a Hindu community was dedicated to or used as of right by the general Hindu community, rather than being a denominational temple for that community.
material_facts: The temple was founded by families belonging to one Hindu community, and its trustees had always belonged to that community.
The temple’s landed properties had been endowed by members of that community, with no reliable evidence of immovable-property endowments by outsiders.
Witnesses from outside the community did not claim a right to worship; their offerings were voluntary and produced little income.
Members of the community alone were allowed to participate in the more important ceremonies.
Other Hindus were not prevented from worshipping, but the evidence did not establish that their use was as of right.

The High Court treated references to the temple’s general body and evidence of outside worship and offerings as supporting public dedication, but the Supreme Court found those inferences unsupported by the evidence.
issues.conclusion: The evidence did not establish that the general Hindu community used the temple as of right or that it was dedicated to that community. The temple was a denominational or sectional temple belonging to the relevant Hindu community, and the trial court’s decision was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6(17) of the Madras Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1951, a temple includes a place dedicated to, for the benefit of, or used as of right by the Hindu community or any section of it. Free admission of the public does not by itself justify an inference of dedication to the public; the evidentiary value of public use depends on circumstances supporting the inference that the use was as of right. The Court relied on Bihar State Board Religious Trust, Patna v. Mahant Sri Biseshwar Das, [1971] 3 SCR 680, 689.

rule.if: civil_appeal_on_temple_status and temple_founded_and_managed_by_one_hindu_section and temple_properties_endowed_by_that_section and outsiders_did_not_claim_a_right_to_worship and important_rites_limited_to_that_section

predicates.civil_appeal_on_temple_status: The proceeding was a civil appeal concerning whether a temple was public or belonged to a Hindu section.
predicates.temple_founded_and_managed_by_one_hindu_: Families of one Hindu section founded the temple, and members of that section managed it as trustees.
predicates.temple_properties_endowed_by_that_sectio: Members of that Hindu section endowed the temple’s landed properties, and no reliable evidence showed outsiders endowed immovable property.
predicates.outsiders_did_not_claim_a_right_to_worsh: Witnesses from outside the section did not claim a right to worship, and their offerings were voluntary and small.
predicates.important_rites_limited_to_that_section: Members of the section were allowed to participate in the more important ceremonies.

issues.definition: When an appeal about a temple’s status involves a temple founded and managed by one Hindu section, endowed by its members, with outsiders not claiming a right to worship and important rites limited to the section, the temple is sectional rather than dedicated to general public worship.
